questions.question_text: How many undergraduate course preferences can you include in a single UAC application?
options: Up to 3
Up to 5
Up to 10
Unlimited
questions.explanation: The standard UAC undergraduate application allows you to select up to five course preferences.

questions.question_text: If you receive an offer in an early round, what should you do if you want to be considered for your higher preferences in later rounds?
options: Accept the offer and leave your preferences as they are
Decline the offer immediately
Remove the successful course from your preferences list
Call the university to request a transfer
questions.explanation: Removing the course you were offered prevents it from blocking future offers to higher-listed preferences in later rounds.

questions.question_text: How many undergraduate course preferences are you generally allowed to include in a single UAC application?
options: Up to 2
Up to 3
Up to 5
Up to 10
questions.explanation: A single undergraduate UAC application allows you to include up to five course preferences.

questions.question_text: If you receive an offer in an early round, what should you do if you still want to be considered for your higher preferences in later rounds?
options: Do nothing and wait
Delete the course you were offered from your preferences
Withdraw your entire application
Accept the offer and leave the course as your first preference
questions.explanation: To remain eligible for higher preferences in future rounds, you should remove the course you have already been offered to prevent it from blocking offers to your higher-listed preferences.

questions.question_text: How often can you change your course preferences through UAC?
options: Only once per month
You cannot change them once submitted
As often as you like, free of charge
Only when you receive an offer
questions.explanation: Applicants are free to change their course preferences as often as they wish at no additional cost throughout the admissions period.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to list your most desired course as your first preference?
options: Because institutions only look at the first preference
Preferences are considered in the order you list them
It is a legal requirement of the government
It determines the application fee amount
questions.explanation: Course preferences are evaluated in the order they are listed. If you are eligible for a higher preference, you will receive an offer for that course, and lower preferences will not be considered.

questions.question_text: What happens if your course preference status is 'competing with other applicants'?
options: You have been rejected
You have met basic requirements but are waiting to see if your selection rank is high enough for an offer
You need to pay an extra fee
You are automatically guaranteed a place
questions.explanation: This status means you are eligible but must wait to see if you rank high enough against other applicants to receive an offer.
